newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Zeitler - investment not yet helping economy.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Zeitler - investment not yet helping economy.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Franz-Christoph Zeitler said on Monday that private investment has not yet emerged as a motor of economic growth, despite generally favourable economic conditions.

"Despite a favourable environment for prices, interest rates and currencies, private investment has not yet sprung to life as an economic motor, the spark from exports has not yet jumped to investment," Zeitler said according to a statement.
The Bundesbank official, who is also president of the state central bank in Bavaria, called on the government to cut spending in order to make room for lower taxes and social security contributions.
A summary of his remarks was made available to the media in advance of the speech.
Zeitler also said that Maastricht Treaty criteria should be strictly meet and not fulfilled through temporary measures like "cosmetic operations on budgets."
